open_items: ECB metadata 503 (provider_down): first occurrence, cycle 199 (2026-08-10T18:01:22Z) - gateway metadata and direct metadata both HTTP 503 for /service/dataflow/ECB/all/latest; gateway data, direct data, direct json all stayed ok. Recorded as provider_down in endpoint_status_at_last_run since that was cycle 199's actual status, but a live recheck ~44 min after this run started (data-api.ecb.europa.eu direct, unauthenticated) returned 200 with a normal payload - already recovered by then. Different failure mode than the earlier resolved ECB 406 issue and different from the ECB references:* 504 contract-probe flap (cycles 182-183, item below): this one hit the basic metadata check on both paths, not just references=* probes. The next run should see a fresh cycle showing ECB healthy again and report that as a recovery per the framework (an endpoint returning to healthy is itself reportable) - do not treat that as a new issue, it is this same event closing out. Watch for a second 503 occurrence; if the next episode does not resolve within a cycle or two, escalate.

ABS gateway metadata 502 Bad Gateway flap: new shape, cycle 198 (2026-08-10T16:01:22Z) - only gateway metadata failed, with an actual error message and HTTP 502 from data.api.abs.gov.au; direct metadata/data/json and gateway data all stayed ok in the same cycle. Resolved by cycle 199. This is NOT the same pattern as the long-tracked ABS empty-error-body flap below (which has no error message at all) - here the message and status are both present, and it looks like a genuine transient 502 from ABS's own server surfacing through the gateway. First occurrence of this specific shape; watch for recurrence.

ABS gateway metadata empty-error-body flap: fifth occurrence, cycles 150-152 (3 consecutive cycles, 4 hours), resolved by cycle 153, healthy through cycle 199 (no new occurrence, 48 consecutive healthy cycles for this specific empty-message shape; note cycle 198 had a different ABS gateway_issue with a real error message and 502 status, tracked separately above). Longest occurrence yet (prior max was 2 consecutive cycles, cycles 150-151; before that all resolved within one cycle: cycle 26, cycle 134, cycle 143). Empty error message itself still worth fixing under code-change scope (GatewayError/next_step in monitor/checks_gateway.py). Watch for a sixth occurrence; if it spans 4+ cycles, treat as a genuine regression rather than the known cosmetic pattern.

UNICEF direct-path HTTP 404 'no data found' flap: first occurrence, cycle 197 (2026-08-10T14:01:22Z) - gateway data, direct data, and direct json all returned HTTP 404; metadata unaffected on both paths; constraint:availableconstraint contract assertion also went broken (expected 200, observed 404) in the same cycle. Resolved by cycle 198. Different shape than the tracked UNICEF 429 flap below (which is a rate-limit signal, not a 'no data' signal) - likely a transient empty result for the probe's specific dataflow/period. Watch for a second occurrence of this specific 404 shape.

ILO references:contentconstraint ignored-vs-ok blip: cycle 199 read verdict ok instead of the expected ignored (expected/observed both stayed '200'->'200', so it did not surface in /api/contracts changes, which only diffs those two fields, not the verdict). Live recheck against sdmx.ilo.org/rest/dataflow/ILO/DF_GED_XLU1_SEX_HHT_CHL_RT/latest showed references=none and references=contentconstraint returning identical payload size and content (aside from per-request message:ID/Prepared header fields) - the parameter is still silently dropped in substance, so this reads as one-cycle noise in the monitor's own comparison rather than a real capability change. Not broken or capability_appeared, so not alerted on its own. Watch for recurrence; if it persists across cycles, revisit as a possible real behavior change.

ESTAT list_dataflows timeout pattern: ninth episode (cycles 144-145) resolved by cycle 146, clean through cycle 199 (54 consecutive healthy cycles). No fix applied under docs-only scope; standing recommendation (raise deadline, stream listing, or cache parsed result) carried forward for a session with code-change scope. Watch for a tenth episode, especially one that fails to resolve within a cycle or two.
STATSNZ auth:listing capability_appeared, first seen cycle 60, still present at cycle 199: listing served without credentials. Still open, not re-reported since no new change.

Content-Type parameter order (charset vs version) on structure responses varies between requests, seen on ABS, OECD, ILO, and FBOS. Cosmetic, verdict stays ok. Expected to keep flapping across multiple endpoints; do not re-report unless the verdict itself changes.

ILO direct-path 403 flap: fourth occurrence at cycle 166 (2026-08-08T00:01:22Z) - 5 of 12 contract assertions broken (references:all, children, descendants, parents, parentsandsiblings), resolved within that cycle, clean through cycle 199 (checked cycles 197-199 individually, all healthy, no broken contract rows). Prior occurrences: cycle 32, cycle 94, cycle 159 (broadest yet at 10 of 12). All four resolved within one cycle. Basic gateway/direct health checks stayed healthy throughout every occurrence - only contract-probe traffic drew the 403. IMPORTANT: /api/history's per-endpoint status/failing series does NOT reflect contract-probe-only degradation. Every run must check intermediate cycles individually since the last run via /api/cycle/{id}, not rely on /api/history or /api/contracts changes (which only diffs the two newest cycles) alone.

IMF references:* 401 flap: first occurrence, cycle 161 (14:01:22Z) - 4 of the references:* contract assertions (all, children, descendants, parentsandsiblings) returned HTTP 401 where 200 was expected, resolved by cycle 162, clean through cycle 199 (no recurrence, checked cycles 197-199 individually). Same shape as the recurring ILO 403 flap (probe volume tripping provider-side throttling, not a general IMF outage). Watch for a second occurrence; a second episode soon would elevate this from one-off to a recognized pattern like ILO's.

UNICEF direct-path HTTP 429 flap: second occurrence at cycle 178 (2026-08-09T00:01:22Z) - gateway data, direct data, and direct json all returned HTTP 429; metadata unaffected on both paths. Resolved by the time of that run's live recheck (~40 min later, both direct data and metadata returned 200). First occurrence was cycle 126 (direct data + direct json only), resolved by cycle 127, clean for 51 cycles in between. No 429 recurrence through cycle 199 (cycle 197's UNICEF flap was the different 404 shape tracked above, not 429). Watch for a third 429 occurrence; a third episode soon, or broader/gateway-affecting breadth like the second one, would elevate this from a one-off pair to a recognized recurring pattern like ILO's 403 flap.

ECB references:* 504 flap: first occurrence, spanning cycles 182 and 183 (2026-08-09T09:01:22Z and 11:01:22Z approx) - references:descendants, references:none, references:parents broken at 182 (HTTP 504); references:children, references:contentconstraint broken at 183 (HTTP 504); resolved by cycle 184, clean through cycle 199 (checked cycles 197-199 individually, no recurrence of this specific references=*-only 504 shape). Basic gateway/direct health checks (metadata, data, json) stayed ok throughout - only contract-probe references=* queries timed out. Not the same failure mode as ECB's earlier resolved 406 issue, and not the same as the new ECB metadata 503 at cycle 199 tracked above (that one hit the basic metadata check on both paths, not just references=* probes). Watch for a second occurrence of this specific 504-on-references-only shape; a second episode soon would elevate this from one-off to a recognized recurring pattern.
